description: How to run and trust Coga's test suite and validation from a checkout, the environment and fixture pitfalls, the agent-run verification tiers (no hosted CI), and the exact verification receipts reviewers expect.
---

# Testing Coga

## Commands

```sh
python -m pip install -e ".[test]"   # editable, with pytest, hatchling and pip
coga --help                          # or: python -m coga.cli --help
python -m pytest
coga validate --json                 # or: python -m coga.validate --json
```

Coga needs Python 3.11+ (`tomllib`); an older interpreter fails loud. If pip's
hash-checking mode blocks the editable install, use `uv` or prefix the one
command with `PIP_REQUIRE_HASHES=0`. A venv made with `uv venv` (or
`python -m venv --without-pip`) initially has no `pip`; `uv sync --extra test`
or `uv pip install -e ".[test]"` installs all test tools, including pip. Run
`coga validate --json` after config, workflow, or task-model changes.

**Validate `tests/fixtures/seeded-repo/coga` with `env -u SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL coga validate --json`**
when your shell exports that variable. The fixture has notifications off, and
the config-load guard rejects a bare exported `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` with no
`webhook` key (the shipped `coga.toml` notification comments). Unset the
variable for the one command; do not edit the fixture's config to satisfy it.

**A repo-wide `coga validate` refuses a shebang script that is not
executable** (`non-executable-script`); the user-facing rule, remedy, and
mode sources live in [coga/first-task](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/first-task/SKILL.md#0-check-readiness).
When adding a script under `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/`,
commit it `100755` if it starts with `#!`; import-only modules carry no
shebang and stay `100644`. A packaged-tree finding in an adopting repo is
fixed here, upstream; Dream routes it as human-needed rather than a local PR.
The walk skips symlinks and prunes `.git`, `__pycache__`, `node_modules`, and
`.venv` (`validate._check_shebang_executables`).

For artifact-level reproduction, use the
[Linux clean-install harness](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/SKILL.md). It covers current PyPI
and a wheel from `main` in a fresh Python 3.11 container, with an attended
continuation for agent login, the first-run `coga build`, and the first
ticket. The
[macOS harness on AWS](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/macos-aws/SKILL.md) runs the same walk on
an EC2 Mac dedicated host, and the
[Windows harness on AWS](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/windows-aws/SKILL.md) on EC2 Windows
Server. The
[attended human walk](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/coga/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/human-walk/SKILL.md)
is their hand-run counterpart: a first-time user installs on a fresh
`cogatest` VM while an agent records findings.

## Which code you are actually testing

- **Package-owned definitions.** Tests and harnesses read shipped skills,
  workflows and recurring definitions from the package tree
  (`src/coga/resources/templates/coga/...`). The inverse inventory in
  `test_packaging` rejects unapproved live copies, including identical ones;
  required package resources are pinned independently of local state. The
  publication regressions in `test_git` run the control tree's own imports
  and packaging/navigation/runtime checks: the first conversion uses the
  pinned Stage A merge, and final-state dirty/committed package edits must
  stay on the feature branch during a mutating CLI exit sweep. The historical
  transition test needs Git history containing that merge; a shallow checkout
  reports an explicit skip and cannot supply that transition receipt. Pass
  `--basetemp` on a roomy volume for full runs: the suite creates many
  temporary repos and can fill a small `/tmp` tmpfs. Keep that basetemp
  outside the checkout (for example a sibling directory of it): an in-checkout
  basetemp lets the missing-repo tests walk up, discover the checkout's real
  `coga.toml`, and stop testing the no-repo case (observed 2026-11-04).
  On Windows, use a short
  root such as `C:\ct`; nested control checks and wheel copies can otherwise
  exceed MAX_PATH. Control clones disable `core.autocrlf` to preserve pinned
  definition bytes. The Stage A check backports one explicit-LF test-fixture
  write; its product code and assertions remain pinned to the historical tree.

- **Run the suite with an absolute `PYTHONPATH` whenever you are not in the
  primary checkout.** In-process imports are safe: `pyproject.toml` sets
  `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["src"]`, so tests import the
  checkout's own `coga`. Subprocess children (`sys.executable -m coga.cli`,
  `coga`, `ticket.py`) inherit the environment instead, and a healthy editable
  install's `.pth` names one checkout's `src`, so without an exported absolute
  `PYTHONPATH` they run the primary checkout's package: a mixed run where
  in-process assertions exercise your branch and CLI-driven ones do not. Use
  `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src python3.12 -m pytest`. The same spelling recovers when
  the `.pth` points at a deleted worktree.
- `PYTHONPATH` must be absolute (some subprocess tests change cwd). Name a
  3.11+ interpreter explicitly; the ambient `python3` on dev machines is often
  3.9.
- **The `coga` on PATH may be a uv tool editable install**, not a checkout
  venv. Its interpreter is the `python` beside the resolved entry point:

  ```sh
  python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; from shutil import which; print(Path(which("coga")).resolve().parent / "python")'
  ```

  That environment's `coga-*.dist-info/direct_url.json` names the checkout it
  imports, regardless of your cwd. Scripts that must `import coga` against the
  active CLI run under that interpreter. Repoint it (`uv tool install --force
  -e <checkout>`; the tool env has no `pip`) only to the long-lived checkout;
  verify branches with `PYTHONPATH`. A checkout `.venv/` is the test
  environment, not what `coga` on PATH runs. If `src/coga/` edits do not show
  up, check which checkout the install imports.
- **Codex runs its commands in a login shell** (`bash -lc`), which re-reads
  `~/.profile`; one that prepends `~/.local/bin` puts the uv tool `coga` back
  in front of a checkout venv you put first on PATH before launching. To
  dogfood a branch's `coga` under codex (for example a Dream run in a scratch
  clone), set top-level `allow_login_shell = false` in that checkout's
  gitignored `.codex/config.toml` and confirm with `command -v coga` from a
  codex session.
- **Live-test a launch-path branch from a non-editable install.** To exercise
  a branch's launch, supervisor, or capture code in a real `coga launch` or
  `coga chat` session, install the branch commit non-editable into a scratch
  venv and run that venv's `coga` by absolute path (`<venv>/bin/coga launch
  ...`) without activating the venv: launch prepares the control checkout
  (`main`), so an editable install of the checkout would run main's code.
  The agent inherits the supervisor's `PATH` unchanged (`build_launch_env`
  copies the parent environment), so commands it runs inside the session (for
  example `coga mark done`) resolve the `coga` on that `PATH`. Without
  activation only the supervisor/capture side runs the branch; activating the
  venv or prepending its `bin/` would put the branch install on both sides.
  Confirm with `command -v coga` from the session, and read the results with
  that split in mind (seen in the 2026-10-15 Codex SIGINT reproduction).
- Installed-versus-source skew warnings from `launch`/`validate` are owned by
  [coga/launch](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/launch/SKILL.md).

## Test-writing rules

- Name tests after the command or module (`tests/test_launch.py`). Coga's own
  bundled ticket scripts are exercised from `tests/` against `tests/fixtures/seeded-repo/`.
- **Launch metadata is scrubbed for you.** `tests/conftest.py`
  `_clear_supervised_session_env` clears `LAUNCH_OWNED_ENV`, derived from
  `coga.task_env.TASK_ENV_KEYS`, so a worker cannot write into the outer
  launched ticket. Add new launch-owned variables to `TASK_ENV_KEYS`; do not
  add per-test `delenv` opt-outs. `tests/test_env_isolation.py` proves it.
- **Do not pin to live dogfooded state.** Files under `coga/` mutate as the
  repo is used. Strip runtime fields or freeze the period; assert structure.
- **Fixture shell scripts must be portable.** Avoid GNU-only `sed -i`,
  `readlink -f`, `date -d`; prefer Python or `sed ... > tmp && mv tmp file`.
- **Stand in for a tool interpreter with an `exec` wrapper, not a symlink.**
  Python finds `pyvenv.cfg` beside the path it was invoked by, so a symlink
  to `sys.executable` placed elsewhere runs the base interpreter without the
  venv's packages; globally installed packages then hide the loss.
  `tests/test_clean_install_harness.py` `_tool_python` writes a `/bin/sh`
  wrapper that `exec`s the quoted interpreter, and its regression test
  imports a module present only in a throwaway venv so no global package can
  stand in.
- **Native Windows fixtures use UTF-8 and LF explicitly.** `conftest` isolates
  HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA and the temp variables. Fixture
  paths are resolved to their canonical spelling, including HOME and TEMP,
  so a reused directory with different username casing matches Git's path
  reports on Windows. `init_git_repo` disables `core.autocrlf` for ordinary
  fixtures. Dedicated Git tests still exercise CRLF clean filters.
  A fresh child interpreter does not inherit pytest's monkeypatches. Launch
  fixtures that fake the supervisor inside that child must also fake the
  Windows CLI resolver there, so command planning can reach the simulated
  agent without requiring an installed agent CLI.
  `write_executable` supplies a
  Python shebang on POSIX and a `.cmd` launcher on Windows. Use
  `remove_test_checkout` when a fixture deliberately removes a Git clone;
  Git for Windows marks object files read-only.
- **All Windows exclusions use `conftest.windows_skip(reason)`.** A POSIX
  PTY-mechanics test (`pty.fork`, `TIOCSWINSZ`, SIGWINCH, fork gates) may skip
  only when its reason names the Windows-run equivalent of the same contract,
  usually in `tests/test_repl_supervisor_nt.py`. Keep
  mocked orchestration tests running; skip only actual PTY/agent behavior,
  POSIX modes or Unix host/runbook scripts, and list every non-interactive
  exclusion with its reason in the PR. Native locks and Job Object recovery
  tests must run on Windows, without externally enabling Python UTF-8 mode.
  This repository keeps `.gitignore` LF because Git for Windows can interpret
  CR-only blank ignore lines as matches; this does not change init's policy
  for adopting repositories.
- **A test that models an agent must fake one of the agent seams.** Fake
  `shutil.which` (installed agent), `subprocess.run` (the agent run), or
  `coga.launch.run_with_done_marker`. The Windows planner resolves the agent
  against the child's PATH/PATHEXT and spawns it through `ProcessTree`, so
  without a fake a native run starts the real installed `claude.exe`; native
  runs once found about 126 orchestration tests doing so. The autouse
  `tests/conftest.py` `_windows_agent_spawn_follows_test_fakes` keeps the
  bare CLI name while one of those seams is faked and routes the no-console,
  ungated Windows spawn through a faked `subprocess.run`, matching POSIX. Only
  `tests/test_repl_supervisor_nt.py`, which owns the real Windows spawn
  contract, is exempt.
- **`coga.config` and `coga.launch` share one `subprocess` module
  object.** Use one argv-dispatching mock on `coga.config.subprocess.run`.
- **Scope standard-library mocks to the operation under test.** For example,
  restore `shutil.get_terminal_size` with `monkeypatch.context()` before
  pytest reports the result; pytest also calls it with `fallback=`.
- **Symlink-loop rejection has interpreter-dependent diagnostics.** Python
  3.12 raises while resolving the cyclic contexts root; Python 3.14 leaves
  it unresolved with `strict=False`, so configuration rejects it at the
  subsequent symlink traversal check. Tests must require rejection while
  accepting either diagnostic, as `test_layout_contexts_cyclic_root_rejected`
  does.
- `hatchling` is a tracked test extra, not a runtime dependency, because
  `tests/test_packaging.py::test_wheel_includes_bootstrap_batteries` builds
  with `--no-build-isolation` and fails (not skips) without it; see
  [coga-dev/packaging](../packaging/SKILL.md). The wheel tests shell out to
  `python -m pip`, so `pip` is also an explicit test extra for uv-created
  environments that otherwise omit it.

## Known suite failures

Rule these out before blaming the change under test.

- **The full suite can exhaust `/tmp` inodes.** Each run creates thousands of
  fixture repositories. On a `/tmp` with free bytes but few free inodes, one
  run ended with 1,413 passed, 10 skipped and 2,708 errors, with 36 inodes
  left. Check `df -i /tmp`, remove only that run's fixtures, and rerun with
  `TMPDIR` on the main disk.
- **`control_relay_started` leaks between tests (open, no ticket).**
  `recurring_runner` sets the `git.control_relay_started` ContextVar when it
  relays to a control worktree, and nothing resets it between tests. Running
  `tests/test_recurring.py::test_recurring_scan_relays_into_existing_control_worktree`
  before
  `tests/test_git.py::test_recurring_all_child_retains_the_control_worktree_sweep`
  fails the second one: `_sweep_coga_state` makes no sync call
  (`assert 0 == 1`). Reproduced on control on 2026-11-02. The default
  full-suite order passes, so the failure only shows up in reordered or
  focused selections. Confirm by running the failing test alone.
- **A Windows checkout and temp directory on different drives** break
  `os.path.relpath`, which raises `ValueError` across drives. A path computed
  between package resources and a fixture repo must fall back to an absolute
  target, as `agent_skills` does for skill links. The retired hosted Windows
  runner (package on `D:`, temporary repos on `C:`) failed 228 tests this
  way; the Windows AWS harness's default layout keeps both on `C:`, so it
  does not exercise this split.

## Verification tiers and receipts

**Coga has no hosted test CI** (owner decision, 2026-11-05). Agents and the
release operator run every check on real machines. The only workflow is the
publish-only `.github/workflows/release.yml`
([coga/releasing](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/releasing/SKILL.md)).
It builds, runs `twine check` (metadata only), and uploads. It runs no tests.

History, so nobody re-adds CI without the reasons: a 2026-09-24 no-CI policy
was reversed on 2026-10-23 by PR #1097, which added a `Test` workflow running
the suite on Linux and Windows for every pull request and every push to
`main`. Automatic ticket/log publication turned that into repeated full runs,
and a packaging-twin inconsistency (live blocker-reminders template published
before its package twin) made every run fail and notify. The owner disabled
the workflow on 2026-10-26 and deleted it on 2026-11-05
(`v1/13-repair-ci-and-resume-with-release-focused-triggers`). The tradeoff:
nothing mechanical blocks a merge or an upload. Verification is a
procedure enforced by the implementer, the reviewer and the release
operator. In exchange there are no hosted runs, queues or failure
notifications, and platform checks run natively on the AWS harnesses.

**Native checks are release-only** (owner decision, 2026-11-12). Windows
and macOS full-suite receipts are required before release, not for
implementation, peer review or merge, including platform-sensitive changes.
Do not allocate native test hosts as a routine PR gate. This concentrates
native verification on the release candidate; the tradeoff is that a native
regression may first be found during release preparation and must be fixed
before tagging.

1. **Every change.** Implement, self-QA and review steps run the full suite
   locally (Linux) and record receipts.
   Record native verification as deferred to release in the PR and ticket,
   when present; Linux receipts do not provide native Windows or macOS
   evidence.
2. **Every release, before tagging.** Run the full suite at the exact commit
   to be tagged on Linux, natively on Windows through the
   [Windows AWS harness](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/windows-aws/SKILL.md#long-native-runs),
   and natively on macOS through the
   [macOS AWS harness](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/testing/clean-install/macos-aws/SKILL.md#full-suite-at-a-commit),
   plus the build, `twine check` and clean-install checks. Record the receipts
   with the release ticket. [coga/releasing](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/coga/releasing/SKILL.md)
   owns the release procedure. A failure or missing receipt on any platform
   means no tag. A changed release commit needs new receipts; earlier PR
   receipts do not substitute for verification of that commit.

**Python 3.11 floor evidence.** At least one release suite run uses a real
Python 3.11 interpreter, Coga's `requires-python` floor. Examples are the
Linux clean-install harness's Python 3.11 container, or the Windows
harness's `checkout`, which syncs the test environment with a uv-managed
Python 3.11 (`uv sync --python 3.11 --extra test`). A green 3.12 run
is not evidence for the floor. For per-change checks, when 3.11 is unavailable,
report that gap with the actual interpreter and results. Reusable workflows
cannot assume Python 3.11 is installed in a user's environment. Raising
`requires-python` requires an owner decision.

**Receipt fields.** Each run records the full commit SHA, the platform and OS
version, the Python version, the exact command, pass/skip/fail counts, and
runtime. For example: `3f1c…` (full SHA), Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12.12,
`PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src .venv/bin/python -m pytest` -> `4058 passed, 10 skipped`
in 410s. "Tests pass" with no command and counts is not evidence. A receipt
is evidence for exactly its commit, interpreter and platform. Runs on
uncommitted changes count for a commit only when the committed tree is
identical.

**Local-run environment.** The POSIX migration-runbook test requires ripgrep
(`rg`) on PATH. Set `TERM=dumb` when output formatting matters (for example
under a forced-terminal environment), so Typer does not insert ANSI codes
into plain-text assertions. The suite does not run `coga validate`,
interactive launch (checked on EC2), or anything needing a real agent CLI,
network or AWS; such tests must skip cleanly rather than be excluded.
Windows skips about 90 more tests than Linux. The native Windows run exists
for behavior that differs there (paths, processes, locks, encoding), not for
extra Windows-only tests.

- **Verify fix claims by exact token.** A done ticket's claim that it fixed a
  failing test is not proof of what reached `main` (a half-applied fixture fix
  once stayed red for weeks while four tickets re-diagnosed it). Check with
  `git log -S'<exact token>' -- <test file>` and the absolute-`PYTHONPATH`
  run, and record a partial fix as half-applied, not absent.
- **Scope validation with `coga validate --task <slug>`.** The repo-wide run
  has no known error baseline: its last standing error sat on a draft now
  parked under `_v2/`, which validation never reads. Any repo-wide error is a
  real change, not drift to report and move on from.

## Reviewer test environment

- **`codex review`'s own test attempt is expected to fail collection** (for
  example `No module named 'tomlkit'`): it runs pytest under an ambient
  interpreter without Coga's dependencies. That is not a finding against the
  branch and does not void the review verdict. Run the suite yourself with a
  Coga-capable interpreter (`PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src .venv/bin/python -m pytest`)
  and record that command and count as the evidence.

description: Authoring Coga's packaged resources, enforcing user versus local-only Coga-dev contexts, single-source ownership, and wheel contents, including the README as the PyPI long description.
---

# Packaging Coga's resources

## Where bundled resources live

Bundled skills, contexts, reusable workflows, and command tickets are authored
under `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/`. Runtime resolvers
(`paths.resolve_context_path`, `resolve_skill_path`, `resolve_workflow_path`,
`tasks.resolve_bootstrap`) check the repo first and then read the package; no
`coga/bootstrap/` mirror is materialized. Optional domain skills are not
packaged; operators install them with `coga skill install`
([coga/skill-management](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/skill-management/SKILL.md)).

**Local-first also applies to this repo.** A live `coga/<kind>/<name>`
shadows the packaged copy; where none exists, the packaged file is what this
repo resolves and freezes. This repo has no live `coga/workflows/code/`, so
editing `bootstrap/workflows/code/*.md` changes what `mark_active` freezes into
Coga's own tickets. Check which side is live before assuming an edit is
downstream-only.

## Distribution states for a context

- **Bootstrap fallback**: `templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/<ref>/SKILL.md`
  (every `coga/*` topic). `coga init` skips `bootstrap/`;
  `paths.resolve_context_path` reads the package copy
  (`bootstrap_context_path`) when the repo has no local `<ref>/SKILL.md`.
- **Init-seeded**: `templates/coga/contexts/**`, today only the scaffolds
  `.gitignore` and `_template/SKILL.md`. `commands/update.py`
  `copy_fresh_templates` copies only the reviewed `FRESH_SCAFFOLDS`
  allowlist once; nothing reads the packaged original at runtime.
- **Local-only**: no packaged copy, resolved first and unknown to other repos
  (a repo's `product/` topics, or this repo's `coga-dev/` set).

Resolution is local, then `bootstrap/contexts/`, then `None`, which `compose`
turns into a `ComposeError`. Skills and workflows have the same split:
fallback only from `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`. Every reusable workflow
and skill, including `direct/body`, `build/onboarding` and the recurring
workflows, is now a bootstrap battery; `templates/coga/{skills,workflows}/`
hold only the ignored `_template` starters. A present but unusable local
override (`paths.local_definition_entry`) raises `LocalOverrideError` rather
than selecting the packaged copy.

**Bundled launchers may only name fallback contexts.** A bundled
`bootstrap/<verb>/ticket.md`, or a bundled skill that tells the agent to apply
a context, must name contexts that resolve from `bootstrap/contexts/`, because
an init-seeded copy may be pruned or predate the repo.
`tests/test_packaging.py::test_bundled_bootstrap_tickets_attach_only_bootstrap_contexts`
enforces this.

## Package ownership and repo state

The audience criterion belongs to
[context layout](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences):
user topics operate shipped surfaces; Coga-dev topics explain developing Coga.
The complete `coga-dev/` namespace, including attachments, stays local. A
shipped surface may not require it; optional development navigation uses an
absolute GitHub link.

Every shipped definition has one committed owner under `src/coga/resources/`.
This repo has completed its cutover: user topics live only in package
`bootstrap/contexts/`, reusable skills/workflows in `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`,
and recurring definitions with their scripts/runbooks in `recurring/<name>/`.
Indexes link directly to those owners. The configured `docs/contexts/` root
holds local Coga-dev knowledge. There are no forwarding files or symlink mirrors.

`tests/test_packaging.py` owns the executable inventory:

- `_discover_live_packaged_twins()` derives every possible counterpart from
  the actual package tree, including top-level prompt overrides and both
  ordinary and obsolete bootstrap locations. `_ownership_problems()` rejects
  every unapproved counterpart, even byte-identical files.
- `tests/required_package_resources.txt` independently pins required package
  files. Removing both an owner and a local copy cannot make the test pass;
  new/retired resources need a deliberate manifest update. Bootstrap context
  refs remain pinned separately by `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_CONTEXT_REFS`.
- `SCAFFOLD_COUNTERPARTS` explains required physical configuration, context,
  audit log, attribute and ignore files. `INTENTIONALLY_DIVERGENT_TWINS`
  explains actual differences from their seeds. This repo selects packaged
  trim-log in `coga/recurring/jobs.toml`; its physical log attribute matches
  the package seed. Adoption and removal of the old attribute exception
  belong in the same reviewed change.
- `STATE_CARRIER_COUNTERPARTS` explains saved recurring parent blackboards.
  `inspect_parent_dir` requires the exact carrier shape and rejects leftover
  definition siblings. `LAZY_STATE_CARRIER_COUNTERPARTS` names the adopted
  trim-log parent, which may be absent until its first admitted run creates
  state; any present copy still requires the exact carrier shape. Arbitrary
  blackboard notes remain state even without declared `state_keys`;
  phone-home's complete cursor is independently parsed.
- `LOCAL_DEFINITION_OVERRIDES` requires a reason for every retained definition
  counterpart. It is currently empty. An ambiguous customization is retained
  for owner review, never silently deleted. All exception entries must name
  real current files except the explicitly lazy state carrier above; stale
  reasons fail. Repo-only jobs and attachments have no packaged counterpart
  and stay local.
- Authoring starters may exist only as ignored, untracked materializations.
  `.coga/`, `.venv/`, generated agent views, bytecode caches and local config
  are machine-local artifacts outside the definition inventory.
- Navigation reads actual package-relative links and inbound links from local
  development topics, repo-authored skills/workflows/jobs, indexes and release
  notes. Frozen task histories and archives are excluded; archives are never
  read by the check.

The generic migration and rollback contract belongs to
[the recurring runbook](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/templates/package-definitions-migration.md).
Its source-repo rehearsal retained every parent blackboard, worklist, frozen
period, custom job and clone ledger. Publication continues to use the ordinary
state roots and guards. Package edits are outside those roots; deliberately
reviewed local knowledge edits on a feature checkout are held for merge,
dirty or committed, so commit them on the branch. See [state publication](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/state-publication/SKILL.md).

A packaged recurring template leaves `owner:` and `agent:` empty so each
adopting repo's defaults apply; `test_recurring` pins that routing. A local
full fork owns all its siblings, while a carrier reads the package's definition.
The Coga repo keeps only root `AGENTS.md`; Claude Code reads it when no
`CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` exists. Do not recreate a second root guide.

## Wheel packaging

`[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]` in `pyproject.toml` walks
`packages = ["src/coga", "src/coga_edge"]` and force-includes pure-data trees. Hatchling's walk
silently drops no-`.py` skill directories, so `bootstrap/` and
`skills/_template` are excluded from the walk and force-included as their
single shipper. A walk and a force-include of the same file abort the build
("A second file is being added to the wheel archive at the same path").

This fails only on a pristine tree: in a dev tree, gitignored agent symlink
views under the templates tree dedup the collision away. The wheel tests
therefore build from a pristine copy of the tracked files
(`test_packaging._pristine_source`), assert no archive path ships twice, and
smoke-test the installed, read-only artifact outside the source tree.
Build artifacts (`.coga/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`) are excluded so a dirty
tree cannot ship a stale venv into every `coga init`.

`README.md` is also the package's PyPI long description
(`readme = "README.md"` in `pyproject.toml`). PyPI does not resolve relative
links, so every README link must be an absolute GitHub URL: `blob/main/...`
for files and `tree/main/...` for directories. Done tickets are retired, so
link evidence such as a ticket file or a `coga/log.md` excerpt at a commit
(`blob/<sha>/...`), not at `main`.

# PR presentation and preparation record

Part of [coga/pr-publication](../SKILL.md).

## Presentation and review-depth rubric

The preparation agent chooses an advisory depth; the owner always decides
whether to merge. Titles use `[<depth> · A:<author> R:<reviewer>] <change>`.
Use actual session/tool identities and receipts, never ticket assignments or
the GitHub publisher. `unknown` means unavailable evidence, `none` means no
review, and `<name>(self)` distinguishes self-review from independent review.
The complete title stays within GitHub's 256-character limit: retain the
prefix and shorten an oversized change title with an ellipsis. The full change
title remains in the body, and the literal ticket snapshot stays unshortened.

| Depth | Judgment and representative evidence | Example title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `merge` | Small, low-risk, fully understood change; independent review returned on this diff, applicable checks passed, no unresolved concerns or deviations. Tests alone never suffice. | `[merge · A:codex R:claude] Fix help-text typo` |
| `skim` | Bounded, understood change; read the description for a tradeoff or limitation. Explain why the recorded verification suffices; disclose self-review and justified omissions. | `[skim · A:claude R:codex] Clarify retry diagnostics` |
| `deep` | Inspect the diff: significant behavior/risk, uncertainty, unresolved findings, failed/pending checks, absent review or missing evidence. | `[deep · A:codex R:none] Change PR publication behavior` |

A typo example can use a passed rendered-help comparison with a reason the
runtime suite is inapplicable. The diagnostics example can use passed focused
error-path tests and a completed independent review, with broader tests omitted
because execution behavior is unchanged. The publication example warrants deep
review even with green tests because it changes evidence and overwrite rules;
if independent review was not performed, say why. These are examples of agent
judgment, not a risk classifier in Python. Workflow test/review obligations
remain in force; publication adds no universal suite gate.

## Preparation record

The last judgment step reads this section and writes one fenced `yaml` mapping
under `## PR` on the blackboard (ticket-body `## PR` is a legacy location).
The section holds only that fence up to the next `##` heading; any prose,
horizontal rule, or second block makes `coga open-pr` refuse with "use one
complete fenced yaml mapping under ## PR".
Implement records actual authorship and checks; the final review step refreshes
it after the final freshness/rebase pass, fixes, and required checks. Prepare
the record last so its head/base and receipts describe the resulting revision.
Design approval is not code review. Do not copy a
configured identity, infer execution from a planned command, or re-stamp an old
receipt. Resolve the full feature OID with `git rev-parse <branch>` and the
reviewed diff base with `git merge-base origin/main <branch>`. Every executed
check and review has its own `head` and `base`; omit those only for `not-run`.

```yaml
title: Explain retry failures without changing retry behavior
author: claude
author_evidence: Implement session used Claude; see implement handoff.
head: <full feature commit OID>
base: <full merge-base OID>
depth: skim
rationale: Bounded diagnostics change; read the description for the wording choice.
implementation: Adds the exhausted-attempt count to the existing diagnostic.
deviations: None; retry behavior is unchanged.
limitations: No interactive terminal rendering check; plain stderr only.
files:
  src/retry.py: Expose the attempt count in the failure diagnostic.
  tests/test_retry.py: Cover exhausted retries and unchanged successful retries.
review:
  reviewer: codex
  kind: independent
  status: passed
  head: <full reviewed feature commit OID>
  base: <full reviewed merge-base OID>
  detail: Codex review returned with no unresolved findings.
checks:
  - command: python -m pytest tests/test_retry.py
    status: passed
    head: <full tested feature commit OID>
    base: <full tested merge-base OID>
    detail: 12 passed.
  - command: python -m pytest
    status: not-run
    detail: Workflow permits focused checks; only diagnostic wording changed.
```

`files` maps every path in the actual base-to-head diff to why it belongs,
including both old and new names for a rename. Identical explanations can
repeat. `review.kind` is `independent`, `self`, or `none`; check/review status
is `passed`, `failed`, `pending`, or `not-run`. Every receipt needs a detail
(result/counts or reason for omission). With no independent review, use self
or none and explain why; do not turn an absent tool into a passed review.

Write every free-text value (`rationale`, `implementation`, `deviations`,
`limitations`, `author_evidence`, each `detail`, each `files` explanation) as
a folded block scalar (`>-`) or a quoted string: a plain scalar containing
`: ` or starting with `[` or `{` is invalid YAML, and `coga open-pr` refuses
it. `review` is always a nested mapping, never a string, and `depth` is exactly
`merge`, `skim`, or `deep`.

The formatter enumerates paths using Git's NUL-delimited rename-aware diff.
The file table shows only each path and its change type (`M`, `A`, `D`, or the
rename/copy status). Per-file explanations stay in preparation as coverage
evidence; they are not repeated in a Why column. Missing preparation paths
are reported as unexplained; extra prepared paths are reported as outside
the current diff. The body starts with
the recommendation/rationale, then authorship/review, implementation,
deviations/limitations, every file, and actual check receipts. Checks are a list:
each result or omission reason comes first, with its command in a separate
fenced shell block below, so long commands do not squeeze the explanations
into table columns. A separate collapsible section renders the ticket title
and the complete Description and Context as Markdown, preserving their source
text, excluding frontmatter, blackboard and PR preparation. The snapshot has no
outer code fence: its headings, lists, links and own code blocks render normally.
Snapshot extraction happens at publication.
The closure marker remains machine-readable outside that snapshot.

Missing/unstructured preparation publishes a `deep` fallback with unknown
identity and explicit missing implementation, file, test and review evidence.
Legacy free-form `## PR` prose is shown as unverified implementation text,
never as check or review evidence. An empty blackboard `## PR` does not shadow
a populated ticket-body one. Malformed YAML or fields refuse with a repair
message. A top-level head/base mismatch is a visible stale-preparation gap that
forces `deep` but keeps the prepared explanations; each receipt is judged
against its own head/base, and stale ones are displayed as historical, not as
verification of the current diff. An `independent` review whose reviewer equals
the author is shown and judged as self-review. Missing or stale evidence, unexplained paths,
and failed/pending checks force `deep`; `merge` also requires a passed independent
review and at least one passed applicable check. Reasons for unrun checks stay
visible; deciding applicability remains the preparation agent's job.

# Packaging Coga's resources

## Where bundled resources live

Bundled skills, contexts, reusable workflows, and command tickets are authored
under `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/`. Runtime resolvers
(`paths.resolve_context_path`, `resolve_skill_path`, `resolve_workflow_path`,
`tasks.resolve_bootstrap`) check the repo first and then read the package; no
`coga/bootstrap/` mirror is materialized. Optional domain skills are not
packaged; operators install them with `coga skill install`
([coga/skill-management](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/skill-management/SKILL.md)).

**Local-first also applies to this repo.** A live `coga/<kind>/<name>`
shadows the packaged copy; where none exists, the packaged file is what this
repo resolves and freezes. This repo has no live `coga/workflows/code/`, so
editing `bootstrap/workflows/code/*.md` changes what `mark_active` freezes into
Coga's own tickets. Check which side is live before assuming an edit is
downstream-only.

## Distribution states for a context

- **Bootstrap fallback**: `templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/<ref>/SKILL.md`
  (every `coga/*` topic). `coga init` skips `bootstrap/`;
  `paths.resolve_context_path` reads the package copy
  (`bootstrap_context_path`) when the repo has no local `<ref>/SKILL.md`.
- **Init-seeded**: `templates/coga/contexts/**`, today only the scaffolds
  `.gitignore` and `_template/SKILL.md`. `commands/update.py`
  `copy_fresh_templates` copies only the reviewed `FRESH_SCAFFOLDS`
  allowlist once; nothing reads the packaged original at runtime.
- **Local-only**: no packaged copy, resolved first and unknown to other repos
  (a repo's `product/` topics, or this repo's `coga-dev/` set).

Resolution is local, then `bootstrap/contexts/`, then `None`, which `compose`
turns into a `ComposeError`. Skills and workflows have the same split:
fallback only from `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`. Every reusable workflow
and skill, including `direct/body`, `build/onboarding` and the recurring
workflows, is now a bootstrap battery; `templates/coga/{skills,workflows}/`
hold only the ignored `_template` starters. A present but unusable local
override (`paths.local_definition_entry`) raises `LocalOverrideError` rather
than selecting the packaged copy.

**Bundled launchers may only name fallback contexts.** A bundled
`bootstrap/<verb>/ticket.md`, or a bundled skill that tells the agent to apply
a context, must name contexts that resolve from `bootstrap/contexts/`, because
an init-seeded copy may be pruned or predate the repo.
`tests/test_packaging.py::test_bundled_bootstrap_tickets_attach_only_bootstrap_contexts`
enforces this.

## Package ownership and repo state

The audience criterion belongs to
[context layout](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/context-layout/SKILL.md#context-audiences):
user topics operate shipped surfaces; Coga-dev topics explain developing Coga.
The complete `coga-dev/` namespace, including attachments, stays local. A
shipped surface may not require it; optional development navigation uses an
absolute GitHub link.

Every shipped definition has one committed owner under `src/coga/resources/`.
This repo has completed its cutover: user topics live only in package
`bootstrap/contexts/`, reusable skills/workflows in `bootstrap/{skills,workflows}/`,
and recurring definitions with their scripts/runbooks in `recurring/<name>/`.
Indexes link directly to those owners. The configured `docs/contexts/` root
holds local Coga-dev knowledge. There are no forwarding files or symlink mirrors.

`tests/test_packaging.py` owns the executable inventory:

- `_discover_live_packaged_twins()` derives every possible counterpart from
  the actual package tree, including top-level prompt overrides and both
  ordinary and obsolete bootstrap locations. `_ownership_problems()` rejects
  every unapproved counterpart, even byte-identical files.
- `tests/required_package_resources.txt` independently pins required package
  files. Removing both an owner and a local copy cannot make the test pass;
  new/retired resources need a deliberate manifest update. Bootstrap context
  refs remain pinned separately by `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_CONTEXT_REFS`.
- `SCAFFOLD_COUNTERPARTS` explains required physical configuration, context,
  audit log, attribute and ignore files. `INTENTIONALLY_DIVERGENT_TWINS`
  explains actual differences from their seeds. This repo selects packaged
  trim-log in `coga/recurring/jobs.toml`; its physical log attribute matches
  the package seed. Adoption and removal of the old attribute exception
  belong in the same reviewed change.
- `STATE_CARRIER_COUNTERPARTS` explains saved recurring parent blackboards.
  `inspect_parent_dir` requires the exact carrier shape and rejects leftover
  definition siblings. `LAZY_STATE_CARRIER_COUNTERPARTS` names the adopted
  trim-log parent, which may be absent until its first admitted run creates
  state; any present copy still requires the exact carrier shape. Arbitrary
  blackboard notes remain state even without declared `state_keys`;
  phone-home's complete cursor is independently parsed.
- `LOCAL_DEFINITION_OVERRIDES` requires a reason for every retained definition
  counterpart. It is currently empty. An ambiguous customization is retained
  for owner review, never silently deleted. All exception entries must name
  real current files except the explicitly lazy state carrier above; stale
  reasons fail. Repo-only jobs and attachments have no packaged counterpart
  and stay local.
- Authoring starters may exist only as ignored, untracked materializations.
  `.coga/`, `.venv/`, generated agent views, bytecode caches and local config
  are machine-local artifacts outside the definition inventory.
- Navigation reads actual package-relative links and inbound links from local
  development topics, repo-authored skills/workflows/jobs, indexes and release
  notes. Frozen task histories and archives are excluded; archives are never
  read by the check.

The generic migration and rollback contract belongs to
[the recurring runbook](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/recurring/templates/package-definitions-migration.md).
Its source-repo rehearsal retained every parent blackboard, worklist, frozen
period, custom job and clone ledger. Publication continues to use the ordinary
state roots and guards. Package edits are outside those roots; deliberately
reviewed local knowledge edits on a feature checkout are held for merge,
dirty or committed, so commit them on the branch. See [state publication](../../../../src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/state-publication/SKILL.md).

A packaged recurring template leaves `owner:` and `agent:` empty so each
adopting repo's defaults apply; `test_recurring` pins that routing. A local
full fork owns all its siblings, while a carrier reads the package's definition.
The Coga repo keeps only root `AGENTS.md`; Claude Code reads it when no
`CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` exists. Do not recreate a second root guide.

## Wheel packaging

`[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]` in `pyproject.toml` walks
`packages = ["src/coga", "src/coga_edge"]` and force-includes pure-data trees. Hatchling's walk
silently drops no-`.py` skill directories, so `bootstrap/` and
`skills/_template` are excluded from the walk and force-included as their
single shipper. A walk and a force-include of the same file abort the build
("A second file is being added to the wheel archive at the same path").

This fails only on a pristine tree: in a dev tree, gitignored agent symlink
views under the templates tree dedup the collision away. The wheel tests
therefore build from a pristine copy of the tracked files
(`test_packaging._pristine_source`), assert no archive path ships twice, and
smoke-test the installed, read-only artifact outside the source tree.
Build artifacts (`.coga/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`) are excluded so a dirty
tree cannot ship a stale venv into every `coga init`.

`README.md` is also the package's PyPI long description
(`readme = "README.md"` in `pyproject.toml`). PyPI does not resolve relative
links, so every README link must be an absolute GitHub URL: `blob/main/...`
for files and `tree/main/...` for directories. Done tickets are retired, so
link evidence such as a ticket file or a `coga/log.md` excerpt at a commit
(`blob/<sha>/...`), not at `main`.

# PR presentation and preparation record

Part of [coga/pr-publication](../SKILL.md).

## Presentation and review-depth rubric

The preparation agent chooses an advisory depth; the owner always decides
whether to merge. Titles use `[<depth> · A:<author> R:<reviewer>] <change>`.
Use actual session/tool identities and receipts, never ticket assignments or
the GitHub publisher. `unknown` means unavailable evidence, `none` means no
review, and `<name>(self)` distinguishes self-review from independent review.
The complete title stays within GitHub's 256-character limit: retain the
prefix and shorten an oversized change title with an ellipsis. The full change
title remains in the body, and the literal ticket snapshot stays unshortened.

| Depth | Judgment and representative evidence | Example title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `merge` | Small, low-risk, fully understood change; independent review returned on this diff, applicable checks passed, no unresolved concerns or deviations. Tests alone never suffice. | `[merge · A:codex R:claude] Fix help-text typo` |
| `skim` | Bounded, understood change; read the description for a tradeoff or limitation. Explain why the recorded verification suffices; disclose self-review and justified omissions. | `[skim · A:claude R:codex] Clarify retry diagnostics` |
| `deep` | Inspect the diff: significant behavior/risk, uncertainty, unresolved findings, failed/pending checks, absent review or missing evidence. | `[deep · A:codex R:none] Change PR publication behavior` |

A typo example can use a passed rendered-help comparison with a reason the
runtime suite is inapplicable. The diagnostics example can use passed focused
error-path tests and a completed independent review, with broader tests omitted
because execution behavior is unchanged. The publication example warrants deep
review even with green tests because it changes evidence and overwrite rules;
if independent review was not performed, say why. These are examples of agent
judgment, not a risk classifier in Python. Workflow test/review obligations
remain in force; publication adds no universal suite gate.

## Preparation record

The last judgment step reads this section and writes one fenced `yaml` mapping
under `## PR` on the blackboard (ticket-body `## PR` is a legacy location).
The section holds only that fence up to the next `##` heading; any prose,
horizontal rule, or second block makes `coga open-pr` refuse with "use one
complete fenced yaml mapping under ## PR".
Implement records actual authorship and checks; the final review step refreshes
it after the final freshness/rebase pass, fixes, and required checks. Prepare
the record last so its head/base and receipts describe the resulting revision.
Design approval is not code review. Do not copy a
configured identity, infer execution from a planned command, or re-stamp an old
receipt. Resolve the full feature OID with `git rev-parse <branch>` and the
reviewed diff base with `git merge-base origin/main <branch>`. Every executed
check and review has its own `head` and `base`; omit those only for `not-run`.

GIT-LS-REMOTE(1)                  Git Manual                  GIT-LS-REMOTE(1)

NAME
       git-ls-remote - List references in a remote repository

SYNOPSIS
       git ls-remote [--heads] [--tags] [--refs] [--upload-pack=<exec>]
                     [-q | --quiet] [--exit-code] [--get-url] [--sort=<key>]
                     [--symref] [<repository> [<patterns>...]]

DESCRIPTION
       Displays references available in a remote repository along with the
       associated commit IDs.

OPTIONS
       -h, --heads, -t, --tags
           Limit to only refs/heads and refs/tags, respectively. These options
           are not mutually exclusive; when given both, references stored in
           refs/heads and refs/tags are displayed. Note that git ls-remote -h
           used without anything else on the command line gives help,
           consistent with other git subcommands.

       --refs
           Do not show peeled tags or pseudorefs like HEAD in the output.

       -q, --quiet
           Do not print remote URL to stderr.

       --upload-pack=<exec>
           Specify the full path of git-upload-pack on the remote host. This
           allows listing references from repositories accessed via SSH and
           where the SSH daemon does not use the PATH configured by the user.

       --exit-code
           Exit with status "2" when no matching refs are found in the remote
           repository. Usually the command exits with status "0" to indicate
           it successfully talked with the remote repository, whether it found
           any matching refs.

       --get-url
           Expand the URL of the given remote repository taking into account
           any "url.<base>.insteadOf" config setting (See git-config(1)) and
           exit without talking to the remote.

       --symref
           In addition to the object pointed by it, show the underlying ref
           pointed by it when showing a symbolic ref. Currently, upload-pack
           only shows the symref HEAD, so it will be the only one shown by
           ls-remote.

       --sort=<key>
           Sort based on the key given. Prefix - to sort in descending order
           of the value. Supports "version:refname" or "v:refname" (tag names
           are treated as versions). The "version:refname" sort order can also
           be affected by the "versionsort.suffix" configuration variable. See
           git-for-each-ref(1) for more sort options, but be aware keys like
           committerdate that require access to the objects themselves will
           not work for refs whose objects have not yet been fetched from the
           remote, and will give a missing object error.

       -o <option>, --server-option=<option>
           Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using
           protocol version 2. The given string must not contain a NUL or LF
           character. When multiple --server-option=<option> are given, they
           are all sent to the other side in the order listed on the command
           line.

       <repository>
           The "remote" repository to query. This parameter can be either a
           URL or the name of a remote (see the GIT URLS and REMOTES sections
           of git-fetch(1)).

       <patterns>...
           When unspecified, all references, after filtering done with --heads
           and --tags, are shown. When <patterns>... are specified, only
           references matching one or more of the given patterns are
           displayed. Each pattern is interpreted as a glob (see glob in
           gitglossary(7)) which is matched against the "tail" of a ref,
           starting either from the start of the ref (so a full name like
           refs/heads/foo matches) or from a slash separator (so bar matches
           refs/heads/bar but not refs/heads/foobar).

OUTPUT
       The output is in the format:

           <oid> TAB <ref> LF

       When showing an annotated tag, unless --refs is given, two such lines
       are shown: one with the refname for the tag itself as <ref>, and
       another with <ref> followed by ^{}. The <oid> on the latter line shows
       the name of the object the tag points at.

EXAMPLES
       •   List all references (including symbolics and pseudorefs), peeling
           tags:

               $ git ls-remote
               27d43aaaf50ef0ae014b88bba294f93658016a2e        HEAD
               950264636c68591989456e3ba0a5442f93152c1a        refs/heads/main
               d9ab777d41f92a8c1684c91cfb02053d7dd1046b        refs/heads/next
               d4ca2e3147b409459955613c152220f4db848ee1        refs/tags/v2.40.0
               73876f4861cd3d187a4682290ab75c9dccadbc56        refs/tags/v2.40.0^{}

       •   List all references matching given patterns:

               $ git ls-remote http://www.kernel.org/pub/scm/git/git.git master seen rc
               5fe978a5381f1fbad26a80e682ddd2a401966740        refs/heads/master
               c781a84b5204fb294c9ccc79f8b3baceeb32c061        refs/heads/seen

       •   List only tags matching a given wildcard pattern:

               $ git ls-remote --tags http://www.kernel.org/pub/scm/git/git.git v\*
               485a869c64a68cc5795dd99689797c5900f4716d        refs/tags/v2.39.2
               cbf04937d5b9fcf0a76c28f69e6294e9e3ecd7e6        refs/tags/v2.39.2^{}
               d4ca2e3147b409459955613c152220f4db848ee1        refs/tags/v2.40.0
               73876f4861cd3d187a4682290ab75c9dccadbc56        refs/tags/v2.40.0^{}

NAME
       git-ls-remote - List references in a remote repository

SYNOPSIS
       git ls-remote [--heads] [--tags] [--refs] [--upload-pack=<exec>]
                     [-q | --quiet] [--exit-code] [--get-url] [--sort=<key>]
                     [--symref] [<repository> [<patterns>...]]

DESCRIPTION
       Displays references available in a remote repository along with the
       associated commit IDs.

OPTIONS
       -h, --heads, -t, --tags
           Limit to only refs/heads and refs/tags, respectively. These options
           are not mutually exclusive; when given both, references stored in
           refs/heads and refs/tags are displayed. Note that git ls-remote -h
           used without anything else on the command line gives help,
           consistent with other git subcommands.

       --refs
           Do not show peeled tags or pseudorefs like HEAD in the output.

       -q, --quiet
           Do not print remote URL to stderr.

       --upload-pack=<exec>
           Specify the full path of git-upload-pack on the remote host. This
           allows listing references from repositories accessed via SSH and
           where the SSH daemon does not use the PATH configured by the user.

       --exit-code
           Exit with status "2" when no matching refs are found in the remote
           repository. Usually the command exits with status "0" to indicate
           it successfully talked with the remote repository, whether it found
           any matching refs.

       --get-url
           Expand the URL of the given remote repository taking into account
           any "url.<base>.insteadOf" config setting (See git-config(1)) and
           exit without talking to the remote.

       --symref
           In addition to the object pointed by it, show the underlying ref
           pointed by it when showing a symbolic ref. Currently, upload-pack
           only shows the symref HEAD, so it will be the only one shown by
           ls-remote.

       --sort=<key>
           Sort based on the key given. Prefix - to sort in descending order
           of the value. Supports "version:refname" or "v:refname" (tag names
           are treated as versions). The "version:refname" sort order can also
           be affected by the "versionsort.suffix" configuration variable. See
           git-for-each-ref(1) for more sort options, but be aware keys like
           committerdate that require access to the objects themselves will
           not work for refs whose objects have not yet been fetched from the
           remote, and will give a missing object error.

       -o <option>, --server-option=<option>
           Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using
           protocol version 2. The given string must not contain a NUL or LF
           character. When multiple --server-option=<option> are given, they
           are all sent to the other side in the order listed on the command
           line.

       <repository>
           The "remote" repository to query. This parameter can be either a
           URL or the name of a remote (see the GIT URLS and REMOTES sections
           of git-fetch(1)).

       <patterns>...
           When unspecified, all references, after filtering done with --heads
           and --tags, are shown. When <patterns>... are specified, only
           references matching one or more of the given patterns are
           displayed. Each pattern is interpreted as a glob (see glob in
           gitglossary(7)) which is matched against the "tail" of a ref,
           starting either from the start of the ref (so a full name like
           refs/heads/foo matches) or from a slash separator (so bar matches
           refs/heads/bar but not refs/heads/foobar).

OUTPUT
       The output is in the format:

           <oid> TAB <ref> LF
